stem: In the primary survey of a 4-year-old child after major blunt trauma, which group of observations best assesses the child's breathing (B) component?

options.text: Respiratory rate, chest wall expansion, subcostal/intercostal recession, tracheal tug
Oxygen saturations, skin colour, heart rate, and conscious level
Air entry (equal bilaterally) and added breath sounds
Capillary refill time, blood pressure, and peripheral pulses

explanation: The B component of the primary survey assesses breathing and ventilation. This includes respiratory rate, work of breathing, chest expansion, recessions, and signs of airway obstruction such as tracheal tug. Other options describe oxygenation/perfusion or circulation-focused observations.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: The original item is incomplete and the stem asks about an unclear phrase. Rewritten into a standard single-best-answer question about the primary survey B assessment, preserving the trauma/paediatrics teaching point.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: these are key bedside observations for the breathing assessment in the primary survey.
optionExplanations.B: These are more useful for overall severity and oxygenation/perfusion, but not the core breathing assessment.
optionExplanations.C: Air entry and added sounds are important respiratory findings, but this option is incomplete compared with option A.
optionExplanations.D: These are circulation (C) observations, not breathing (B) observations.

Clinical scenario 1 - James

Teaching/learning points:

Initial ABC approach to trauma patient

Recognition of life-threatening injury and resuscitation priorities

You receive a pre-hospital alert from paramedics regarding James, a four year-old boy who ran away from his mother onto the road, where he was hit by a van at approximately 50kph. He hit the windscreen and was thrown approximately 7 metres. He was unconscious at the scene and not moving spontaneously. The paramedic crew on the scene report him to be unconscious but breathing, with a respiratory rate of 30/min, heart rate 120bpm, multiple abrasions and bruises. ETA 10 minutes.

The following 12 questions refer to James' clinical scenario.
